item.title: Re: Partha Kar: Expanding roles of healthcare staff—where are the safety checks?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Dr Kar writes an excellent piece on concerns that many resident doctors share about the expansion of non-doctor roles in the NHS. There is clearly a role for associated healthcare practitioners in certain fields. item.title: Re: Race is not a biological category: challenging this misconception will help tackle racism in healthcare
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, I welcome Jasmeen Kanwal’s article outlining the importance of rejecting race as a biological category because it leads to patient harm through racism. I wholeheartedly endorse this argument but must challenge the assertion that this is not taught in medical schools or within the canonical medical curriculum. item.title: The PATHWAYS is debate is too important to be left to specialists
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Chris Whitty is wrong to argue that debate on the PATHWAYS trial of puberty blockers in children should be left to specialists. The trial raises deep and important questions: What is it to be male or female? What are the proper limits of medicine? Is it acceptable to treat mental distress by altering healthy bodies? item.title: Re: Roger James Wolstenholme
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Thank you for publishing your obituary of Dr. Roger Wolstenholme. I was very saddened to hear the news of his death. item.title: Re: The growing threat of domestic wood burning stoves—and industry’s legal attempts to shut down clean air campaigns
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, We read with interest the recent BMJ investigation which highlights the health harm caused by wood burning in urban stoves[1]. Such burning also contributes to climate change. Emissions related to logging, sawmill activity, transport and (often) kiln drying can be substantial [2].
